headline: EEG decoding and generative models are tested against held-out stimuli and sham controls
label: Neuroimaging Analysis Validity
summary: New EEG preprints pair cross-modal models with sham controls and unseen stimuli or individuals, probing whether reported decoding gains reflect genuine neural structure.
synthesis: The common thread is whether EEG-based models capture neural structure that generalizes beyond the data used to build them. The contrastive EEG-video study finds alignment outperforms CCA across subjects and seen stimuli but not novel videos, and its sham control shows accuracy can be spurious. EEG-World reports transfer to unseen individuals when forecasting band-power from prior EEG and audiovisual input. The generative framework unifies paired EEG with fMRI BOLD and fNIRS responses to synthesize haemodynamic signals from EEG. NeuroSim offers synthetic EEG with injected disease biomarkers for AD, PD, SCZ, EPI and FTD, aimed at improving classifiers. What is new is the explicit use of sham controls and held-out conditions to separate real signal from evaluation artefacts. All four are preprints, so the findings are preliminary and unreplicated.
